summary:
The July 2026 anti-trans legal risk assessment map places Michigan in its 'Low-Risk States' tier, describing the state as having enacted fairly robust non-discrimination policies while falling short on healthcare equity and on protections for incarcerated transgender people.

Discrimination on the basis of gender identity is unlawful in Michigan under the Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act, following a July 2022 Michigan Supreme Court ruling that affirmed the Attorney General's appeal; the legislature codified the protection in a bill passed in March 2023 and signed by Governor Gretchen Whitmer on 8 March 2023. The ruling built on a 21 May 2018 Civil Rights Commission interpretation adopted 5-0 and on the 7 March 2018 Sixth Circuit decision in EEOC v. R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes holding that Title VII prohibits employment discrimination against transgender people. Sexual-orientation protection followed the same route, from a December 2003 executive order and a March 2013 marina-loan non-discrimination provision through the May 2018 commission interpretation to the March 2023 codification.

Hate-crime law covers gender identity implicitly within Michigan's 1992 hate-crime statute under the category 'gender', per an August 2021 court declaration. A hate-crime package adding 'gender identity or expression' explicitly passed the House in June 2023 and the Senate in December 2024, was signed in January 2025 and took effect 90 days after signature. Sexual orientation has been recognised for hate-crime data collection since 1992.

The gay and trans panic defence was abolished by a law passed, signed and implemented in July 2024.

Conversion therapy is banned statewide under a bill passed by both chambers in June 2023 and signed in July 2023, following a June 2021 executive order barring taxpayer dollars or funding for conversion therapy on minors.

Sex on a Michigan birth certificate can be changed without sexual reassignment surgery under a 30 June 2021 court ruling that declared the 1978 surgery and physician-statement requirement unconstitutional; the position was certified and codified by a bill passed in December 2024. Changing sex on a driver's licence or state ID requires a signed statutory declaration and a fee under the system in place since November 2019.

Marriage between two people of the same sex is legal in Michigan under Obergefell v. Hodges (26 June 2015). Michigan had barred it by a 1995 statute signed by Governor Engler and by the 2004 constitutional amendment Proposal 04-2, approved with 58.6% of the vote, which also barred civil unions. In DeBoer v. Snyder the district court held the ban unconstitutional on 21 March 2014; more than 300 licences were issued on 22 March 2014 before Sixth Circuit stays, and the Sixth Circuit reversed on 6 November 2014.

Michigan's sodomy statute has not been repealed by the legislature even though same-sex sexual activity is legal under Lawrence v. Texas (2003). The statute as written applied to both homosexual and heterosexual conduct, and Michigan and Massachusetts are the only northern states without statutory codification.

The Michigan Supreme Court announced a September 2023 decision on respecting an individual's pronouns for judges.
tangentialFactors: In March 2025 the Michigan House adopted a bipartisan resolution urging the Michigan High School Athletic Association to ban transgender athletes from girls' and women's sports. The measure is advisory and does not change state law or the state's non-discrimination protections. The association has cited potential conflicts between an executive order and the gender-identity non-discrimination provision of the Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act.
localsOnly:
State government employment protections cover gender identity under a 2007 extension and a January 2019 executive order that reaches state employment, contractors and grantees. Insurance companies and corporations are explicitly barred from discriminating on the basis of gender identity under a bill passed by both chambers in October 2023 and signed by Whitmer. An LGBTQ+ Commission was established in June 2023.

Local conversion-therapy bans predate the statewide prohibition, including the August 2020 Royal Oak ordinance, punishable by up to 90 days' imprisonment and a $500 fine.
outOfScopeNotes:
The sources do not confirm whether Michigan driver's licences and state IDs carry an 'X' gender marker. The marker was announced in January 2020 as forthcoming and was still described as 'soon' in November 2021, with no later confirmation in the inventory.

The risk map's finding that Michigan falls short on healthcare equity and on protections for incarcerated transgender people is stated without Michigan-specific detail. No Michigan-specific care restriction, custody policy or enforcement incident appears in the inventory.

The scope of the Michigan Supreme Court's September 2023 pronoun decision is not described beyond judges.

The Michigan legislature has not repealed the sodomy statute; whether repeal is pending is not sourced.

No Michigan-specific data on anti-trans violence or on enforcement statistics was identified in the sources.
